- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.6) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.4), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–4% for next 5–10 days.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 1–3 days); cap forecast increase at +3% after spike.
- Model underestimates mean-reversion periods; if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-period momentum; add 0.5–2% upward bias if sentiment remains positive over last 7 days.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive within 3 days, model lags; forecast should adjust upward by 1–2% within next 2–3 days.
- Model tends to underestimate true price at end of 30-day horizon; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias for final 7–10 days.
